advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a non-timeout CalledProcessError from a git probe still returns None (guarding the TimeoutExpired-before-SubprocessError except ordering).
evidence: ticket cf0f-2e26-87ca-47a8 comment: "TimeoutExpired subclasses the currently caught SubprocessError, so adding only timeout=5 would silently return None; timeout must be separated"
ABSENCE: no test drives a probe to CalledProcessError (nonzero git exit inside a real repo) and asserts the result is still None
advisory.finding: No new test exercises the non-timeout SubprocessError path (e.g. a git probe that exits non-zero -> CalledProcessError) to confirm it still returns None after the change. The ticket explicitly flags that TimeoutExpired subclasses SubprocessError and that the except-clause ordering (TimeoutExpired re-raised BEFORE the SubprocessError->None arm) is load-bearing; only the non-repo/OSError arm is covered (test_head_is_none_outside_a_repo). A regression that reorders or broadens the except arms so a non-timeout failure also raises would not be caught.

coverage.approach_viability_note: 0 surviving high-priority finding(s), Pass-2 drop-rate 67% — the approach (not just nits) may be worth a second look (advisory; the verdict is unchanged).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_stable_subprocess_time` a full proxy of the real `time` module (or subclass with only `sleep` overridden) so no attribute access via `subprocess.time` can raise AttributeError while the probe runs.
evidence: tests/_isolation.py:70: `    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):` — AttributeError is caught by neither clause
dropped.finding: `_stable_subprocess_time` is a SimpleNamespace exposing ONLY `.sleep`. While `subprocess.time` is swapped to it, any access to another attribute of the `time` module through `subprocess.time` (e.g. `monotonic`/`perf_counter`, or on a CPython version/platform whose wait path is module-qualified) raises `AttributeError`, which is neither `OSError` nor `subprocess.SubprocessError`, so it escapes the except clauses in `head`/`porcelain` and crashes the guard instead of returning None or a bounded timeout.
dropped.suggested_fix: Build the shim from the real module, e.g. capture `_real_time = subprocess.time` and construct a proxy that delegates all attributes to it except a stable `sleep`, rather than a SimpleNamespace exposing only `sleep`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the sleep-monkeypatch test actually exercise the swap (assert the probe still times out with `time.sleep` patched AND verify the swap is what prevents the leak) or document that the swap is defensive-only for non-POSIX/other-version paths.
evidence: subprocess timeout deadline uses module global `_time` (monotonic), confirmed present as `subprocess._time`; `subprocess.time.sleep` is not on the POSIX timeout path, so removing the swap would not change this test's outcome

test asserts `assert subprocess.time.sleep is fail_sleep` at test_repo_isolation_guard.py:183 BEFORE the probe, and `assert sleep_calls == []` at :187 after — but never re-checks that subprocess.time was restored to the caller's value after head() returns/raises
ABSENCE: no assertion of the form `assert subprocess.time is <original>` (or `.sleep is fail_sleep`) executed AFTER the bounded probe returns, so removing the finally restoration is undetectable
dropped.finding: The `test_git_probe_timeout_ignores_a_test_monkeypatch_of_time_sleep` test asserts `sleep_calls == []`, but on POSIX CPython the `subprocess.run(timeout=...)` deadline is computed from `subprocess._time` (bound to `time.monotonic`) and the POSIX wait path does not call `time.sleep`; the timeout therefore fires regardless of the `subprocess.time` swap, so the test passes vacuously and does not actually prove the swap is load-bearing.
merged_from: No test asserts that _run_git_probe RESTORES subprocess.time after the probe (its finally block). The three new tests only assert behavior DURING the probe (sleep not called, TimeoutExpired surfaced), and the monkeypatch test checks subprocess.time.sleep is fail_sleep only BEFORE calling head(). Deleting the finally-block restoration in _isolation.py:45-46 — which would permanently pin subprocess.time to the stable-sleep namespace and defeat any other in-process code relying on a test's time.sleep patch — would leave all three new tests green. This is the exact contract PS2 was added to protect (leave shared subprocess/time state intact), so the restoration path has regression blindness.
